questions.learningObjective: Distinguish network load balancing from application routing
questions.stem: A team wants CLZ-220 to route /images to one pool and /api to another. Why is the deployed Standard Load Balancer insufficient?

options.A: It requires every backend to have a public IP
options.B: It only supports a single Windows backend
options.C: It distributes TCP flows without inspecting HTTP URL paths
options.D: It must install IIS on the frontend

optionExplanations.A: Private NICs are valid backends; adding public IPs does not provide URL routing.
optionExplanations.B: The lesson associates two backends with its pool.
optionExplanations.C: This lesson's Layer 4 service needs a separate application-aware delivery tier for path routing.
optionExplanations.D: The frontend is a network service; IIS runs inside the backends.

questions.stem: Which CLZ-220 resource supplies the public address used in load_balancer_url?

options.A: The Standard public IP attached to the load balancer frontend
options.B: The dynamic private address on the first VM NIC
options.C: The web subnet's address prefix
options.D: The generated Windows administrator password

optionExplanations.A: The URL uses azurerm_public_ip.lb.ip_address.
optionExplanations.B: Private backend addresses are not the public HTTP endpoint.
optionExplanations.C: A subnet prefix identifies an address range, not a public endpoint.
optionExplanations.D: A credential is unrelated to the frontend address.

questions.stem: A second IIS VM is healthy locally but receives no frontend traffic. Its NIC has no backend-pool association. What must be corrected?

options.A: Change the VM's administrator username
options.B: Increase the public IP's DNS TTL
options.C: Mark the Terraform password output nonsensitive
options.D: Associate its intended NIC IP configuration with the backend pool

optionExplanations.A: Guest identity does not register a NIC in a backend pool.
optionExplanations.B: DNS caching does not establish backend membership.
optionExplanations.C: Secret display settings do not change network relationships.
optionExplanations.D: The rule can select only associated pool members.

questions.stem: CLZ-220 configures a TCP probe on port 80. IIS accepts TCP connections but returns an application error page. What does a successful probe prove?

options.A: The lesson page contains the correct backend identity
options.B: TCP port 80 accepts the probe connection
options.C: Every application dependency is healthy
options.D: HTTPS certificates are trusted

optionExplanations.A: Only an HTTP content test can demonstrate the expected page.
optionExplanations.B: A TCP probe checks connection acceptance rather than the page's content.
optionExplanations.C: A listening port can coexist with failed downstream dependencies.
optionExplanations.D: The configured probe is TCP on port 80, not certificate validation.

questions.stem: Four HTTP requests all show backend 1 while both backends are healthy. Which explanation should be investigated before declaring failure?

options.A: The requests may reuse a TCP flow that stays on one backend
options.B: The load balancer always selects the lowest VM index
options.C: The probe necessarily deleted backend 2
options.D: The outbound rule duplicates backend 1's page

optionExplanations.A: The service distributes flows, so successive requests need not alternate servers.
optionExplanations.B: Its distribution is not based on Terraform's numeric index.
optionExplanations.C: A repeated page does not prove deletion or failed health.
optionExplanations.D: SNAT rules do not rewrite HTTP content.

questions.stem: A backend stops accepting the configured probe. What is the intended effect on new load-balanced flows after failure is detected?

options.A: They are redirected to the backend's public IP
options.B: They automatically reinstall IIS
options.C: They are sent to other healthy pool members
options.D: They make Terraform destroy the VM

optionExplanations.A: These VMs have private NICs, and unhealthy targets are not bypassed this way.
optionExplanations.B: Health probes do not remediate the guest configuration.
optionExplanations.C: Probe health controls eligibility for new flows.
optionExplanations.D: A probe result does not execute Terraform.

questions.stem: Why does CLZ-220 set disable_outbound_snat = true on its HTTP load-balancing rule?

options.A: To block return packets for every HTTP request
options.B: To make the separately declared outbound rule responsible for egress SNAT
options.C: To remove every public frontend address
options.D: To enable URL-based backend routing

optionExplanations.A: Responses to allowed inbound flows still return normally.
optionExplanations.B: The design avoids implicit outbound SNAT from the inbound rule.
optionExplanations.C: The public HTTP frontend remains in the configuration.
optionExplanations.D: SNAT configuration does not add Layer 7 routing.

questions.stem: The backends need to initiate an Internet connection. Which declared resource provides their explicit egress translation in CLZ-220?

options.A: The TCP health probe
options.B: The Windows administrator credential
options.C: The data-snet declaration alone
options.D: azurerm_lb_outbound_rule.web using the backend pool and public frontend

optionExplanations.A: A probe measures reachability; it does not create general egress.
optionExplanations.B: Guest authentication does not supply a network path.
optionExplanations.C: A subnet without an egress service is not explicit outbound connectivity.
optionExplanations.D: The outbound rule maps the pool's private source flows to the frontend IP.

questions.stem: web-snet disables default outbound access in CLZ-220. Why is the explicit outbound rule still important?

options.A: The flag disables all private VNet communication
options.B: Private backends need an intentional path for new Internet-bound flows
options.C: The flag automatically creates NAT Gateway
options.D: Only public HTTP clients use the outbound rule

optionExplanations.A: Private communication is separate from default Internet egress.
optionExplanations.B: Disabling default outbound access removes reliance on implicit egress.
optionExplanations.C: It creates no NAT Gateway resource.
optionExplanations.D: The rule handles connections initiated by backends.

questions.stem: A custom NSG redesign blocks the AzureLoadBalancer service tag on the probe port. What can happen even though client HTTP is allowed?

options.A: The load balancer switches automatically to DNS probes
options.B: The backend pool becomes an Internet DNS zone
options.C: Terraform starts using round-robin HTTP routing
options.D: The probe can mark otherwise reachable servers unhealthy

optionExplanations.A: The configured TCP probe does not become a DNS probe.
optionExplanations.B: NSGs cannot create DNS resources.
optionExplanations.C: Network filtering does not change the service's routing layer.
optionExplanations.D: Probe traffic must reach the backend as well as client traffic.

questions.stem: A backend NSG must allow Internet HTTP clients in CLZ-220. Why is allowing only the public frontend IP as the source insufficient?

options.A: IIS replaces all packet source IPs with its hostname
options.B: The probe grants all clients NSG access
options.C: The load balancer preserves the client source IP on inbound flows
options.D: The backend pool assigns every client a VM administrator account

optionExplanations.A: Application content does not replace packet source addresses.
optionExplanations.B: Health checks do not override NSG policy.
optionExplanations.C: Rules should account for the original client source, not assume proxy source addresses.
optionExplanations.D: Network forwarding does not create guest accounts.

questions.stem: The HTTP frontend times out and every probe reports unhealthy. Which investigation is most relevant?

options.A: Check backend power, IIS readiness, port 80 rules, and pool associations
options.B: Change the Role tag on the public IP
options.C: Disable state locking to force HTTP responses
options.D: Rotate the load balancer resource group name without inspecting health

optionExplanations.A: These are the configured path's essential components.
optionExplanations.B: Tags do not fix a failed TCP path.
optionExplanations.C: Terraform locking is unrelated to packet forwarding.
optionExplanations.D: Renaming resources adds risk without diagnosing the failure.

questions.stem: Terraform has created both VMs, but the IIS extensions are still running. What should a learner do before treating the endpoint as ready?

options.A: Assume VM creation guarantees the lesson page exists
options.B: Remove the probe to make extension installation finish
options.C: Add public IPs to bypass all validation
options.D: Inspect extension status and then verify probe health and HTTP content

optionExplanations.A: The page is installed by a separate extension.
optionExplanations.B: The probe does not control script execution.
optionExplanations.C: Bypassing the intended topology does not verify it.
optionExplanations.D: Guest bootstrap and network health can lag resource creation.

questions.stem: Azure CLI lists the HTTP rule, pool, and probe. What additional evidence proves usable web delivery?

options.A: terraform fmt reports no formatting differences
options.B: The public IP resource has a Project tag
options.C: An HTTP request through the frontend returns the intended lesson page
options.D: The local tfvars filename matches the lesson

optionExplanations.A: Formatting does not test a deployed endpoint.
optionExplanations.B: Tags do not show an application response.
optionExplanations.C: Resource listings describe configuration, while a request exercises the path.
optionExplanations.D: A local filename is not service evidence.

questions.stem: A learner changes the rule's backend_port to 8080 while IIS still listens on 80. What result should they expect?

options.A: The frontend's forwarded traffic will not reach the intended IIS listener
options.B: The load balancer silently changes the IIS binding
options.C: The frontend begins serving HTTPS automatically
options.D: The Terraform count changes to 8080 VMs

optionExplanations.A: The backend port must match the guest listener.
optionExplanations.B: Network rules do not configure IIS.
optionExplanations.C: Port changes do not add TLS termination.
optionExplanations.D: The port is unrelated to resource cardinality.

questions.learningObjective: Keep application errors distinct from transport failures
questions.stem: A client receives an HTTP 502 through CLZ-220. Which conclusion is sound?

options.A: Standard Load Balancer generated its own IIS error page
options.B: An HTTP component produced the status; the Layer 4 load balancer does not generate HTTP error pages
options.C: A 502 proves Terraform state is corrupted
options.D: A 502 always means both Windows VMs are deallocated

optionExplanations.A: The service forwards transport flows rather than serving IIS pages.
optionExplanations.B: Inspect the backend or another HTTP intermediary as well as transport health.
optionExplanations.C: The status alone gives no evidence about Terraform state.
optionExplanations.D: An HTTP response indicates an HTTP component answered.

questions.stem: A production team wants HTTPS using the lesson's Standard Load Balancer. Which additional responsibility remains?

options.A: Store the certificate only in the backend pool name
options.B: Change the health probe to TCP 443 and assume certificates are installed
options.C: Configure TLS at the application or use an approved TLS-terminating delivery service
options.D: Mark the HTTP URL output sensitive

optionExplanations.A: Resource names cannot configure TLS.
optionExplanations.B: A TCP probe does not install or validate a certificate.
optionExplanations.C: Layer 4 forwarding does not manage HTTP certificates for IIS.
optionExplanations.D: Output visibility does not encrypt traffic.

questions.stem: Which part of CLZ-220's implementation is most likely to dominate its ongoing lab cost?

options.A: The local terraform show command
options.B: The two allocated Windows VMs and their managed OS disks
options.C: The Terraform resource labels
options.D: The numeric indexes in state

optionExplanations.A: Inspecting a local plan does not create a running service.
optionExplanations.B: Multiple Windows compute instances and disks dominate the described topology.
optionExplanations.C: Labels are identifiers, not billable Azure resources.
optionExplanations.D: Indexes do not themselves incur cloud charges.

questions.stem: A learner has quota for only one VM of the selected size, but CLZ-220 declares two. What is the prudent next step?

options.A: Remove the health probe so quota checks stop
options.B: Set the public IP allocation to Dynamic
options.C: Apply repeatedly with state locking disabled
options.D: Resolve quota or choose an approved available size before apply

optionExplanations.A: Health probes do not govern compute quota.
optionExplanations.B: IP allocation does not increase VM quota.
optionExplanations.C: Disabling locks cannot create missing quota and risks state races.
optionExplanations.D: The deployment must fit regional VM capacity and subscription limits.

questions.stem: The Windows password output is sensitive in CLZ-220. Which artifact still requires protection?

options.A: Terraform state that can retain the generated password
options.B: The public lesson title alone
options.C: The subnet's RFC1918 address prefix alone
options.D: The CSS theme preference

optionExplanations.A: Sensitive display controls do not remove secrets from state.
optionExplanations.B: The public title is not an administrator credential.
optionExplanations.C: A private prefix is not the generated password.
optionExplanations.D: A theme choice is unrelated to guest secrets.

questions.stem: The TCP probe is healthy but the page cannot reach its database. What improvement belongs in a production design?

options.A: Add meaningful application health checks and dependency monitoring
options.B: Assume a healthy TCP socket proves every dependency
options.C: Increase the public IP's name length
options.D: Replace backend content with the resource-group ID

optionExplanations.A: Transport reachability is narrower than end-to-end application health.
optionExplanations.B: It does not execute the application's dependency paths.
optionExplanations.C: Naming does not expand health coverage.
optionExplanations.D: Page text does not repair dependency health.

questions.stem: The application grows and needs scalable outbound connectivity instead of the lesson's LB outbound rule. Which candidate matches the production guidance?

options.A: An inbound NAT rule for HTTP only
options.B: An additional IIS homepage file
options.C: Removing all explicit outbound configuration
options.D: NAT Gateway or a governed firewall egress architecture

optionExplanations.A: Inbound forwarding is not a general outbound design.
optionExplanations.B: Guest content does not provide egress SNAT.
optionExplanations.C: That makes the path less intentional, not more scalable.
optionExplanations.D: Choose an explicit egress design suited to scale and inspection needs.

questions.stem: Which lesson traffic does allow-http explicitly permit to the Windows backends?

options.A: All inbound ports from the Internet
options.B: Inbound TCP traffic to destination port 80 from Internet sources
options.C: Only outbound TCP to destination port 3389
options.D: Only probe traffic from every private subnet

optionExplanations.A: The rule's destination port is limited to 80.
optionExplanations.B: The rule matches the intended public HTTP teaching path.
optionExplanations.C: Its direction is Inbound and its destination is HTTP.
optionExplanations.D: Its source is Internet, not a list of private subnet prefixes.

questions.stem: Each backend association references a NIC ID and backend pool ID. What does Terraform infer?

options.A: Every association can be created before both resources exist
options.B: All NICs automatically join every load balancer in the subscription
options.C: The association must use the corresponding created NIC and pool
options.D: The public frontend installs Windows on the NIC

optionExplanations.A: Required identities come from those resources.
optionExplanations.B: Membership is explicitly declared.
optionExplanations.C: References establish graph dependencies and pass the correct resource identities.
optionExplanations.D: The relationship is networking, not guest deployment.

questions.learningObjective: Maintain consistent load balancer component references
questions.stem: The frontend IP configuration is renamed from public to edge, but CLZ-220's rules still reference public. What must be corrected?

options.A: Rename the Windows administrator to edge
options.B: Update the rules' frontend_ip_configuration_name references consistently
options.C: Replace the TCP probe with a DNS record
options.D: Attach a public IP directly to every backend instead

optionExplanations.A: Guest usernames do not identify load balancer frontend configurations.
optionExplanations.B: The HTTP and outbound rules must reference the existing named frontend configuration.
optionExplanations.C: DNS records do not repair a missing frontend reference.
optionExplanations.D: Changing the intended topology is unnecessary; correct the component references.

questions.stem: HTTP requests through the frontend work, but a backend-initiated download fails. What should be checked next?

options.A: Outbound rule configuration and that backend's pool membership
options.B: Only the frontend HTTP page wording
options.C: Only the browser's dark theme setting
options.D: Remove the HTTP rule permanently

optionExplanations.A: Inbound delivery does not by itself prove the explicit egress path.
optionExplanations.B: Text content does not establish outbound connectivity.
optionExplanations.C: The browser theme cannot affect backend SNAT.
optionExplanations.D: Destroying ingress does not diagnose outbound failure.

questions.learningObjective: Validate backend variety without requiring alternation
questions.stem: What is an appropriate success criterion for CLZ-220's repeated frontend HTTP requests?

options.A: Every successive request must alternate between backend 1 and backend 2
options.B: Exactly one backend must answer until Terraform is restarted
options.C: Successful responses can show multiple healthy backend identities across distinct flows
options.D: The load balancer must return the generated administrator password

optionExplanations.A: The service does not promise per-request round robin.
optionExplanations.B: Terraform is not a traffic scheduler.
optionExplanations.C: Flow distribution can expose both identities without strict alternation.
optionExplanations.D: Secrets must never be web validation content.

questions.stem: Why does the cleanup sequence save resource_group_name before terraform destroy?

options.A: Saving the name prevents all resource deletion
options.B: The name contains the load balancer's packet routing table
options.C: Terraform destroy needs the HTTP page content as its password
options.D: Outputs may disappear, so the name remains available for the Azure absence check

optionExplanations.A: A PowerShell variable has no deletion lock.
optionExplanations.B: It identifies a resource group.
optionExplanations.C: Deletion uses provider authentication, not page content.
optionExplanations.D: Retaining the target identity supports a precise post-destroy check.

questions.stem: A learner stops IIS and closes the browser after finishing CLZ-220. What remains to be done?

options.A: Destroy the managed lab resources and verify the resource group is absent
options.B: Only clear browser cookies
options.C: Only run terraform fmt again
options.D: Delete the local README while leaving Azure running

optionExplanations.A: Stopping a service does not remove VMs, disks, IPs, or the load balancer.
optionExplanations.B: Cookies do not delete Azure resources.
optionExplanations.C: Formatting is not cleanup.
optionExplanations.D: Removing documentation leaves the billable footprint intact.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish a public endpoint from public backend NICs
questions.stem: Which topology matches the actual CLZ-220 implementation?

options.A: One public IP attached to each backend NIC and no load balancer
options.B: One public load balancer frontend with two private Windows backend NICs
options.C: A private DNS A record acting as a Layer 7 proxy
options.D: A Bastion host terminating every HTTP request

optionExplanations.A: That is not the declared topology.
optionExplanations.B: The public IP belongs to the frontend; pool members use private NIC addresses.
optionExplanations.C: DNS is not the lesson's web distribution component.
optionExplanations.D: Bastion is a management service and is not created here.
